The surah opens with this truth, and it is a great one: everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and in declaring His purity and greatness, it turns attention to the One Allah. This is the account of a people who, despite being People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), disbelieved and broke their covenant. Look how that Being expelled them from their homes. And He gave everything to those who praise Allah night and day. And indeed.

﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ (95 : 1) "And He is the Mighty, the Wise." He provides the kinds of means through which His friends are helped, and He creates circumstances in which His enemies are ruined by their own hands. He is the greatest of the wise in ordaining and planning.

After this, the account of that incident is presented as follows:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 2:

ھوالذی ........................ شدید العقاب (4) (95 : 2 تا 4) "It is He who expelled those among the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah. But the punishment of Allah came upon them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts, so that they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O you who have vision!

And had Allah not decreed exile for them, He would have punished them in this world; and in the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire. That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes Allah - indeed, Allah is severe in penalty."

From these verses it becomes clear that it was Allah who expelled the disbelievers among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering (al-hashr al-awwal). In reality, the doer of everything is Allah, but in this verse the action is attributed directly to Allah. And the impression that comes across is that Allah Himself was leading this operation, and that the hand of divine power was not concealed behind any veil in this campaign. And these expelled people were removed to a land from which they would be gathered (on the Day of Resurrection), so these people will never return to Madinah, and their gathering (hashr) will now take place from the land of their exile.

The direct expulsion of them by Allah, and His scattering them toward another land, is also known from the following verse.

ماظننتم .................... من اللہ (95 : 2) "But Allah came upon them from where they had not expected, and He cast terror into their hearts." Allah attacked them from within their hearts. Their fortresses remained as they were; Allah put fear into their hearts. They opened the doors of their fortresses with their own hands. The power of Allah showed that they did not even have control over themselves. Their hearts were not under their control, and they no longer held mastery over their wills and their plans. They could not even remain steadfast upon their intentions and their plans, let alone remain within their fortresses. They had made every kind of defensive arrangement, but one arrangement remained: that their hearts be firm too. They were heedless of this aspect. Allah shattered their resolve. This is what happens when Allah undertakes a matter. Allah knew from where the attack should be made. He is the All-Knowing of everything and the All-Aware over everything. Therefore neither any cause was needed, nor any apparent means of the kind that exist in the minds of common people. Are not means and resources also provided by Allah? When Allah wills something, its causes come into view in the twinkling of an eye. Just as outcomes and ends are in His hand, so too means and resources are in His hand. For Allah, neither means and resources nor outcomes and ends are difficult. He is the Mighty, the Wise.

The disbelievers among the People of the Book fortified themselves within their fortresses, yet Allah attacked from a direction they never expected, and they had made their fortification. They had arranged the defence of their homes and fortresses, but what happened was that they kept ruining their homes and fortresses with their own hands, and they also gave the believers the opportunity to ruin them.

يخربون ................ المومنين (95 : 2) "They were destroying their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers." With this verse the story of these disbelievers among the People of the Book comes to an end. How admonishing the manner is, and how vivid the portrayal, and the vision so full of movement. Allah attacks them from behind their fortresses, and they themselves begin to tear down their fortresses, and the believers also destroy them, and they too destroy.

Now observe the first comment on this scene:

فاعتبر وا ................ الابصار (95 : 2) "So take warning, O you who have vision." This comment is most fitting; hearts are fully prepared for it, and every reader is also astonished that there were so many plans and yet such defence!

In the next verse it is stated that Allah had decreed that before the Hereafter, in this very world, they would be humiliated and disgraced. There was no way for them to escape.

﴿And were it not ... the Fire﴾ (95 : 3). For them, Allah had decreed exile; had He not, He would have punished them in this world, and in the Hereafter there is the punishment of the Fire for them as well. Therefore, the punishment of Allah was bound to fall upon them, just as it did. Had Allah not decreed this form, it would have come in another form. This worldly punishment was also fixed for them, and the punishment of the Day of Resurrection is certainly destined for them. Why?

This happened because they opposed Allah and His Messenger, and whoever opposes Allah, indeed Allah is severe in punishment (95 : 4). Al-mushaqqah (opposition, or taking the opposite side) means that they went over to the opposing side instead of standing with Allah and taking His side. Standing with Allah would have meant standing with the Messenger of Allah, because that was the side of Allah. The verse ends by saying that whoever opposes Allah thereby also implicitly opposes the Messenger. It is a strange and ridiculous scene when weak servants take a stand against the Lord, the Majestic, and fortify themselves against Allah. It is a most frightening scene, and this verse points to it: that a weak creature among men invites the wrath of Allah. Allah is severe in wrath.

Here there is an important point about the Banu Nadir.

﴿Those of the People of the Book who disbelieve﴾ (95 : 2). This phrase is repeated many times in this surah, because they rejected the religion of Allah that He revealed to Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ). The Jews used to wait for the coming of Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ). Mentioning their attribute of disbelief here was necessary, because this disbelief was the cause of their punishment. It was also intended to show that the Muslims' actions against them had moral justification, since they too were disbelievers like other disbelievers. For this reason the punishment came upon them. Therefore:

The phrase ﴿Those of the People of the Book who disbelieve﴾ (95 : 2) is very purposeful.

After this, the believers are reassured about certain events: first, that these people were disbelievers, and second, that they were enemies of the Messenger and of Allah. Therefore, regarding the date palm orchards that were cut down, burned, or left standing during the military action, Allah's decision is that this happened by the command of Allah. The believers should not be affected by the propaganda that the Jews spread in this regard.

Sayyid Qutb's commentary in Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 5:

"Līnah" (95:5) refers to the finest date palms. These were the best variety of their time, known to all. The Muslims had cut down some of the gardens of the Jews and had left some standing. In their hearts there was a disquiet, namely over cutting them down and over leaving them. Before this and after it, the rule of war for the Muslims remained that burning and destruction should be avoided. Therefore, for the exceptional situation of what happened in this incident, this verse came so that the hearts of the Muslims might be reassured. The verse declared that if you left the gardens unburned and refrained from it, that too was by the permission of Allah, and if you cut them and burned them, that too was by the permission of Allah. For Allah was directly supervising this expedition. Therefore Allah caused the Muslim armies to do this, and through their hands He manifested the chastisement. Thus all these actions took place by His will. Through them Allah wished to humiliate those depraved people. Before their eyes their beloved gardens were falling and burning, and those that were left standing were also a source of regret for them, as they were leaving them behind. It was Allah's will to afflict them with grief in both ways.

Those believers in whose hearts there was disquiet over why this destruction and burning had occurred were reassured and given comfort that this was indeed the will of Allah. Allah does what He wills. As for the Muslims, they were merely instruments in the hand of divine power.

This second paragraph of this surah also takes up a very important question: what is the ruling regarding the property that came into the hands of the Muslims in this incident and was returned to the Prophet (ﷺ), or regarding similar events that occur in later times. That is, property that comes into hand without war and fighting, or situations in which divine power provided wealth for the Muslims, and the Muslims did not undertake any significant military action in it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 6:

"And whatever Allah restored (as fay') to His Messenger from them, you did not spur horses or camels for it, but Allah gives authority to His messengers over whomever He wills, and Allah is over all things competent. Whatever Allah restores to His Messenger from the people of the towns, it is for Allah and the Messenger and for relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler, so that it does not circulate only among the wealthy among you. So take what the Messenger gives you, and refrain from what he forbids you. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment. (It is also) for the poor emigrants who have been expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful. And (it is also for) those who were settled in the abode (of Hijrah) and had adopted the faith before them. They love those who have emigrated to them, and do not find in their breasts any need for what has been given to them, and they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves are in need. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul – it is those who are the successful. And (it is also for) those who came after them, who say: 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, You are Kind and Merciful.'"

In these verses, is the ruling of fay' being stated, or of other wealth like fay'? Moreover, these verses describe a very important characteristic of the Muslim ummah and Islamic society and its enduring condition, which has been the distinguishing feature of the Muslim ummah and its distinctive glory throughout the entire history of the ummah. It is the quality of the ummah that it has held firmly to. By the grace of Allah, at no time has this characteristic been separated from the ummah. This characteristic has never been separated from any generation, any nation, or any individual Muslim of the ummah throughout the long Islamic history. Furthermore, in whichever regions of this world there are Muslims, this characteristic has not been separated from the Muslims in any of those regions, and this is a great truth, upon which one should reflect deeply.

"And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur horses or camels for it, but Allah gives authority to His messengers over whomever He wills, and Allah is over all things competent."

*Awjaftum* (95:6) is derived from *ijjaf*, which means urging a horse to run swiftly. *Rikab* means camels. The Muslims are told that the Banu Nadir left behind property, and they did not spur horses on it nor obtain it by traveling swiftly on camels. Therefore, the ruling on this property is not that of spoils of war (ghanimah). In ghanimah, four-fifths belong to the fighters, and one-fifth belongs to Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the relatives, orphans, the needy, and the travelers. As for the spoils of Badr, Allah decided their matter. The ruling on this fay' is that all of it belongs to Allah, the Messenger of Allah, the relatives, orphans, the needy, and the travelers, and the Prophet ﷺ would dispose of it. The relatives mentioned in the verse refer to the Messenger of Allah's kinsfolk, because charity was not permissible for them, they had no share in zakat, and the Prophet ﷺ left no wealth that heirs could inherit; among them were also poor people with no income. Therefore, a share of the ghanimah's one-fifth was set aside for them, just as a share was set aside for them in fay' and the kinds of property similar to fay'. As for others, their rulings are well known, and these funds were under the special disposal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

This was the ruling of fay' stated in these verses. However, these verses do not confine themselves to this ruling and the circumstances in which it was applied; rather, another reality is also expressed here.

"But Allah gives authority to His messengers over whomever He wills."

Therefore, this is a part of Allah's decree which has come to pass.

"And Allah is over all things competent."

Thus the affairs of the messengers are established as a manifestation of divine decree, and within the workings of Allah's decree the station of the messengers is also defined: the rise and dominance of the messengers is not a matter of chance. The hand of divine power accomplishes this work. Although the messengers are human beings, they are directly connected with Allah, and through them Allah manifests His system of divine decree and destiny in this world. The works the messengers perform, they perform by the permission of Allah, and with Allah they are decreed. They do not even move according to their own desires. They do no deed according to their own will or their own interests. They undertake war, jihad, peace, reconciliation, or hostility only by the command of Allah, and that is the manifestation of divine decree, and Allah's decree becomes apparent through their actions and their movements. And whatever they do is the act of Allah, and Allah has power over every matter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 7:

"Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns, it belongs to Allah and the Messenger, and to the near relatives, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer, so that it does not circulate only among your wealthy. Take whatever the Messenger gives you, and refrain from whatever he forbids you. And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment." (59:7)

This verse explains the ruling mentioned earlier. In stating the reason for this ruling, the verse makes clear that it rests upon a great principle of the economic system of Islam.

﴿So that it does not circulate only among your wealthy﴾ (59:7): In explaining the reason for the ruling, the verse states another supreme principle of the constitutional system of Islam.

﴿Take whatever the Messenger gives you, and refrain from whatever he forbids you﴾ (59:7): Although these two principles appear in the context of the distribution of fay', they are very important principles in both the economic system and the constitutional system of Islam, and upon these two the economic and constitutional systems of Islam are in fact established.

The first principle is the fundamental principle of Islam's economics, and Islam's economic theories are based upon it. Islam recognises private ownership, but it places a restraint and a check upon private ownership. That is, Islam does not grant private ownership such wide freedom that a limited number of wealthy people draw all wealth and interests towards themselves through the force of capital, and wealth circulates among a few elite. Therefore, every situation in which wealth circulates only among the rich is contrary to Islam's economic theory, and it is also contrary to social justice. Within an Islamic society, social and economic relations are so formed that wealth does not circulate only among a few limited people.

Islam established its economic system upon these principles. It made zakat obligatory, which is levied at two and a half percent on both capital and profit. It is levied at 10 or 5 percent on all agricultural produce, and likewise on livestock and on the treasures that are obtained from the earth. This rate is in fact a very great rate. Furthermore, it set aside a fifth for the mujahideen, whether they are poor or rich, whereas fay' is reserved only for the poor. Likewise, Islam made the owner and the cultivator partners in the produce of land, and it gave the imam the authority to take from people whatever wealth exceeds their needs and distribute it among the poor. And if the public treasury (bayt al-mal) is in need, it may fix a share of the public treasury in people's wealth. Then Islam prohibited hoarding (ihtikar) and prohibited riba (usury), and riba and hoarding are both the principal means of concentration of wealth. In short, the economic system of Islam is established upon this great principle: that wealth should not circulate only among the wealthy, but that it should spread to all the poor. And this principle governs private ownership.

Thus Islam permits private ownership, yet it is not a capitalist system. Nor is the capitalist system derived from the Islamic system, for there is no capitalist system except through riba and hoarding. The Islamic system is a unique system which comes from Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. It arose distinct, it moved distinctly, and even today it stands apart from all other economic systems. It is a unique, balanced, just system that takes care of all rights and obligations. And this system is also in harmony with this universe, because the Creator of this universe is Allah, the Creator of man is Allah, and the Creator of this economic system is also Allah.

The second principle is that of the constitutional system of Islam: that the sources of the Shari'ah are God, the Messenger, the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

﴿Take whatever the Messenger gives you, and refrain from whatever he forbids you﴾ (59:7). This is the fundamental principle of Islamic constitution and law. Islam's legal system is derived from the fact that the Shari'ah is from Allah, and that the Messenger brought it from Allah, and that it consists of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. The entire Muslim community, even together with the ruler of the time, is not authorised to contravene the teachings that are in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. If anyone makes a law contrary to the Qur'an and the Sunnah, it will have no legal standing, because such a law loses its very basis of legitimacy from the outset. This doctrine is entirely different from all human constitutions and theories of legislation, because according to those theories the nation is the source of legislation, such that any nation may make for itself whatever law it wishes, and whatever a nation wishes it may make into a constitution and law. Therefore, in the Islamic constitutional system, the source of sovereignty is the Qur'an and the Sunnah, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ presented. The imam is the deputy of the ummah. Neither the imam nor the nation is authorised to oppose the Shari'ah of Muhammad ﷺ brought by the Messenger of Allah.

Now, if a matter is not addressed in the Qur'an and the Sunnah, it shall be resolved in the light of other principles of the Qur'an and the Sunnah, in such a way that it does not contravene any principle present in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. These principles are not against the Shari'ah; rather, they too are a Shari'ah principle. Therefore, in every case the source of law is the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and other laws and rules are valid only when they do not contradict any established principle of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. The authority of the ummah is confined within this principle. It should be remembered that the imam of the ummah too is bound by this principle. This is a unique system of law, and no human society has any such legal system. It is a system in which the legal order, like the order of the universe, is a natural order, just as Allah has established a natural order for the universe, so too He has established a system of Shari'ah for human beings, so that the law made by man does not clash with the order of nature. And every law that humans have made until now has clashed with the order of nature.

These two principles are linked in this verse to Allah, and people are invited to fear Allah in obeying them.

﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾ (59:7). This is the great guarantee that Islamic law enjoys, so that no one attempts to break it, and there is no room to escape from it, because the believers know that Allah sees, is aware of deeds, and that all people will return to Him, and that if it is violated, He is severe in punishment. They know that wealth must be spread and must not circulate only among the rich, and that they must take what Allah and His Messenger have given in the commands of the Shari'ah, and must abstain from what has been forbidden, and in this matter there is to be no negligence and no laxity, because they will have to stand before Allah.

Now the Messenger of Allah distributed this fay' among the Muhajirun, and included only two poor Ansar in it. This was a particular measure, and its purpose was precisely that wealth should not merely accumulate among the wealthy.

﴿So that it does not circulate only among your wealthy﴾ (59:7). The ruling was general: that it is for the poor, whether they be Muhajirun, Ansar, or those who came after them. Accordingly, the subsequent verses speak of this.

The Qur'an does not state its rulings merely like a dry act. It gives them in a living and general manner of expression. It is a living command that is enforced upon living human beings, and within the command its moral dimensions and causes are also given.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 8:

لِلْفُقَرَاءِ ... الصَّادِقُونَ (59:8) "For the poor emigrants who have been expelled from their homes and their properties. They seek the bounty of Allah and His pleasure, and they stand firmly in support of Allah and His Messenger. It is they who are the truthful."

This is a picture in which the features of the emigrants are clearly drawn. They were deprived of their homes and wealth. Because of the persecution and harshness of the polytheists, and the cold indifference of their relatives and family, they had to leave their homes, and their only fault was that they professed the pure creed (kalima tayyiba) and recognised none but Allah as their Lord.

يَبْتَغُونَ ... وَرِضْوَانًا (59:8) "They seek the bounty of Allah and His pleasure." Their trust is in Allah alone. They live by depending on Him alone, and they are certain that there is no refuge other than Him. And despite this, they are engaged in defending the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

وَيَنصُرُونَ ... وَرَسُولَهُ (59:8) "and they stand firmly in support of Allah and His Messenger." With their hearts and with their swords. And even in extremely difficult circumstances they discharged this duty.

أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ (59:8) "It is they who are the truthful." These are the people who uttered the word of faith with their tongues and then confirmed it through their deeds. They were truthful with Allah in that they chose Him; truthful with the Messenger of Allah in that they obeyed him; and they were also sincere to truth, because in them truth was seen walking and moving.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 9:

﴿And those who had already settled in the abode (of Hijrah) and had embraced faith before them﴾ "those who, before the arrival of the Muhajirin, had embraced faith and were settled in the abode of Hijrah." That is, in Madinat al-Rasul (ﷺ), it was the Ansar who had embraced faith and were settled there. In this way they also settled faith there. It is as if Madinah was the abode of faith and certainty. This is a most beautiful allusive expression. It is the best picture of the attitude the Ansar adopted regarding faith. It was the home of faith, it was the homeland of faith, where the hearts of the believers were attached and where their hearts and souls found tranquility. Returning there they felt at rest, just as a person feels at ease when he comes home. Therefore Madinah was Dar al-Iman (the abode of faith).

﴿They love those who have emigrated to them, and they find not in their breasts any need for what the emigrants were given, and they give them preference over themselves, even though they themselves are in privation﴾ "They love those who came to them migrating, and they do not feel even a need in their hearts for whatever is given to them (the Muhajirin)." In the history of mankind there is no collective event in which a people welcomed emigrants in the way the Ansar welcomed the Muhajirin in Madinah, with great love, selflessness, generosity and kindness. They shared their wealth with them, housed them in their homes and accepted all their responsibilities. It is related in the narrations that no Muhajir stayed in an Ansari's house by nomination; rather, lots were drawn for each person, because whenever a Muhajir arrived, many would come forward saying, "He will stay with us."

﴿And they find not in their breasts any need for what they were given﴾ That is, in cases where the Muhajirin were given more, and the whole of the fay' was reserved for them, they did not feel any need in their hearts because of it. Here the word for narrowness or envy is not used. This points to the purity of their hearts, that they do not feel within their hearts any need, want, or any desire whatsoever.

﴿And they give them preference over themselves, even though they themselves are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, it is those who are successful﴾ Narrowness of the heart is a psychological disease. It closes every door of goodness, because in some form it demands financial sacrifice, demands the suppression of emotions, demands the expenditure of effort, and sometimes even demands the giving of one's life on the path of goodness. A miser can never perform a righteous deed; he is always preoccupied with taking. The world is nothing, and the one who is saved from narrowness of heart has, as it were, a great obstacle removed from before him, and he moves forward spending and giving generously in works of goodness. This is a very great success.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 10:

﴿And those who came after them say: "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and put not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful."﴾ (59:10)

This is the third picture, the picture of people who are most pure, content with Allah's decree, and wise. They are those who came after the Muhajirun and the Ansar. At the time this verse was revealed, they were not present in Madinah. Yet they were already present in Allah's eternal knowledge, which lies beyond the bounds of time and place, and they were to come later into the world. Allah described their qualities in advance: they are people who turn towards Allah. They seek forgiveness not for themselves alone but for the righteous predecessors (salaf salihin), they keep their hearts clear towards all believers, and they pray that their hearts may be clean. This is because there is a bond of faith between them. Allah's mercy has descended upon both of them, in that He has made them believers. And Allah is Ra'uf and Rahim.

These verses show how radiant the face of this Ummah is, and how far-reaching the light it spreads in this universe. Its bond of faith is so strong that its beginning is linked and tied to its end, and its last part is tied to its first part. They are guarantors, protectors, lovers and merciful to one another. Regardless of race and lineage, and regardless of the distance of time and place, they are connected with one another. This Ummah Muslimah remained continuously dominant over the consciousness of Muslims. Thus the believers, until the Day of Judgement, remember those who went before them...

﴿Those who came before them with faith﴾ (59:10) is remembered, and Muslims remember this Ummah in the same way as a person remembers his brothers, with the utmost honour, dignity and love. The predecessors cared for those who would come after them, and those who come after remember their predecessors. They are all one row, one regiment, though ages have passed. They have one banner, one goal, one horizon, and they have one Lord who is Ra'uf and Rahim.

This is that luminous picture before which eyes are dazzled, yet it stands like a living reality. And this Ummah is a most excellent example for humanity: a most noble and generous example for all mankind, as beautiful as anyone can imagine. This picture appears especially beautiful when we study it comparatively alongside a nation of our own age. The nation of our era has come into being on the foundation of Karl Marx's gospel, "Capital." It is a nation in whose hearts hatred and enmity surge. Classes are seen fighting against one another and killing each other. According to the conception of this nation, human history is a picture of war, conflict and hatred, and moreover this nation holds enmity towards all followers of religion.

Once again, compare the Ummah of Muhammad with the nation of Karl Marx. The Ummah of Muhammad raises humanity to its highest ranks, whereas that other nation drags humanity down to the lowest depths of disgrace. The picture of the Ummah of Muhammad is that, beyond the bounds of time and place, free from the boundaries of race and homeland, and outside the limited circles of lineage and family, it makes all human beings guarantors, protectors, friends and well-wishers of one another, and it raises them all towards one lofty goal, which is the worship of Allah... Mahmud and Ayaz stand in one row... whose hearts are pure, and between the earlier and later there is no enmity; they are sympathisers of one another and have pure hearts towards one another.

Whereas the other picture is that people are seen slaughtering one another, some deceive others, exploit them and plot against them; in response, others harbour rancour, envy and hatred towards them. The entire human history is composed of the expression of hatred. Even in places of worship there is hatred. In their view, even prayer is in reality a trap, and religion is a deception through which the wealthy exploit the poor. Looking at these two pictures, read this verse again:

﴿Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and put not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful.﴾ (59:10) This is the caravan of faith, and this is the prayer of the people of faith. It is a most honourable caravan, and this is the prayer of a most open-hearted person.

After this beautiful portrayal, and after placing it upon the most elevated station within a frame of light, the discourse now turns to the subject for which this Surah was revealed. Here there appears a generous picture of another group: the group of the hypocrites (munafiqun):

Here a record is presented of the things that were said between the Jews and the hypocrites of Madinah concerning this incident. The hypocrites did not fulfil the agreements they made with them, and in this way they left the Jews utterly humiliated. Allah attacked them and struck them with such awe that they carried out with their own hands the task which the believers were supposed to carry out. But when the Qur'an presents this record, in every verse it also makes the Muslims aware of a great truth. That truth settles in their hearts, creates a deep impression within them, deepens faith in their minds and hearts, increases their knowledge, and firms up their moral training.

The first truth that is recorded is that the Jews and the hypocrites are brothers to one another.

﴿Have you not considered those who played the hypocrite, saying to their brothers who disbelieve among the People of the Book...﴾ (59:11). "Have you not seen those who have adopted the way of hypocrisy? They say to their disbelieving brothers from among the People of the Book..." So these People of the Book were disbelievers, and the hypocrites were their brothers, even though they had wrapped themselves in the cloak of Islam.

Then the very emphatic assurance that the hypocrites gave to their brethren.

Layin ukhrijtum ... la-nansurannakum (59:11): "If you are expelled, we will certainly go out with you, and in your affair we will never obey anyone; and if you are fought against, we will surely help you."

But Allah knows their reality well. He declares their pact to be entirely different from what they state, and presents a reality that is the very opposite of their emphatic assurances.

Wallahu yashhadu ... yunsarun (59:11-12): "But Allah bears witness that these people are absolute liars. If they are expelled, they will never go out with them; and if they are fought against, they will never help them; and even if they do help them, they will turn their backs, and then they will find no help from anywhere." Thus it happened exactly as Allah had testified. Of the decisions they had made and the declarations they had announced, they did not act on a single one of them.

After this, Allah makes the Muslims aware of the reality that is firmly lodged in the hearts of these hypocrites and of these disbelievers among the People of the Book.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 13:

"Indeed, you are more fearful [of them] in their hearts than of Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand" (59:13). Their condition is that they fear the believers more than they fear Allah. If they feared Allah, they would not fear any of Allah's servants, because fear and awe (khashyah) are one. It is not possible for someone to fear Allah and also fear people. Honour belongs to Allah alone, and all other creation has no honour or dominance in the presence of Allah. All other creatures are subject to Allah's commands. The Qur'an says:

"There is no creature crawling upon the earth but that Allah holds its forelock" (11:56). Therefore, the one who fears Allah does not fear anyone else. But those who do not grasp this truth fear other than Allah, and they fear other powers more than they fear Allah.

"That is because they are a people who do not understand" (59:13). After this, another reality established in their hearts is described, which is the result of the previous reality, namely the fear of the Muslims. This reality too is seated in the hearts of these hypocrites and disbelievers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 14:

"They will not fight against you all together, except in fortified townships or from behind walls. Their hostility among themselves is severe. You think them united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not use their reason." (59:14)

This is one of the miracles of the Qur'an: the picture it drew of the hypocrites and the People of the Book remains true to this day. Whenever and wherever the hypocrites and the disbelieving People of the Book have confronted one another, this very scene has appeared before us. Recently, in the clashes between the Muslim Brotherhood and the Jews on the soil of Palestine, the Jews never came out openly into the field anywhere. They kept fighting while hidden within their settlements and enclaves, and whenever they came out for a short while, they turned their backs and fled like rats. It appeared as though this verse had been revealed about them.

"Glory be to God... the All-Aware" (59:14 onwards). Beyond these realities, their psychological portrayals are also remarkable.

"Their hostility among themselves is severe" (59:14). "You think them united and their hearts are divided" (59:14). In contrast, the condition of the believers is that they are bound to their righteous predecessors who came centuries before them. Despite the distances of time and place, they are tied together by the rope of faith. And in this path, ethnicity, homeland and clan are not obstacles.

"That is because they are a people who do not use their reason" (59:14). Sometimes outward circumstances deceive. The People of the Book appear extremely united and mutually supportive, backing and aiding one another, just as the hypocrites gather on a single platform. But a true report comes from the heavens that the stars are not as they appear. This is merely their external appearance. At times this veil is lifted and their reality becomes visible, showing how deeply divided they are within. And the truthfulness of the Qur'an is confirmed: within one front and one bloc they fight against one another. In fact, they are each striving for their own interests; they hold contradictory desires and their policies clash. Whenever the believers have acted with sincerity, and whenever their hearts have been united upon Allah, rifts have appeared in the front of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and their hearts have scattered apart. Their apparent unity has become a troubled dream. And whenever the believers have shown patience and steadfastness, they have seen that the outward unity and bond among the disbelievers has been exposed, their alliance has crumbled, and it has become clear that among them there are severe disagreements and bitter enmity, and that they are plotting and fighting against one another. Their hearts are completely separated (shatta) from one another.

The disbelievers and hypocrites gain dominance over the Muslims and can inflict harm when the hearts of the Muslims become separated from one another. At that time they no longer present the example of the Muslims described in the previous verse, but are Muslims in name only. Otherwise, regarding the hypocrites in contrast to the believers, the Qur'an said:

"Their hostility among themselves is severe" (59:14). "You think them united, but their hearts are divided" (59:14). The Qur'an firmly instills this reality in the hearts of the believers so that the awe of the disbelievers may be removed from their hearts, and they may not fear them, because their true state is indeed this. Therefore this is training for the Muslims and rests upon an established reality. If Muslims take the Qur'anic teachings seriously, their enemies' affairs will become easy for them, their hearts will unite, and no power in the world will be able to stand against them.

Those who have truly believed in Allah should understand well their own reality and the nature of their enemies. If they have grasped their own reality, half the battle has been won. The Qur'an points to this reality through an event, and it mentions this reality as an illustration and a lesson. Then it analyzed that event and gave arguments so that those who witnessed that event would take heed, and it would become a lesson-giving event for those who came later. The Qur'an made this allusion before those who were aware of this reality. The event of Banu Nadir was not the first; before it there had occurred the event of Banu Qaynuqa. To this the Qur'an alludes:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 15:

﴿Like those who were before them, not long ago, and they tasted the evil consequence of their conduct; and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ (59:15)

The incident of Banu Qaynuqa' took place before the Battle of Badr. There was a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Muslims gained victory over the polytheists at Badr, the Jews found this very disagreeable. They did not accept this great victory of the Muslims in their hearts, and they burned with envy. They thought that the more the Muslims grew in strength in Madinah, the more their own importance diminished. Reports of what they said in this regard kept reaching the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that they were planning some mischief. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) admonished them many times and warned them of the consequences of treachery. They gave a very harsh reply to the admonition of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which contained a threat hidden within it. They said: "Muhammad, do you think that we are like your people, the Quraysh? Do not be deceived into pride that you fought a people who had no experience of war and so you overcame them. We are such that, by God, if you fight us, you will come to know what kind of people we are."

After this, they began to provoke the Muslims. It is related in the narrations that an Arab woman came with some goods and sold them. She sold these goods in the market of Banu Qaynuqa'. After that she sat down with a goldsmith, and they intended to molest her and asked her to uncover her face; she refused. The goldsmith, acting mischievously, tied the lower part of her sheet to her back. When she stood up, her private parts were exposed. They laughed at her. She cried out for help. A Muslim man rose up and killed the goldsmith. All the Jews gathered and killed the Muslim man. Then the Muslims called out for help against the Muslims. The Muslims became very angry over this, and war broke out between them and Banu Qaynuqa'.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them until they laid down their arms on the condition that they would accept whatever decision he made. Then the chief of the hypocrites, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, stood up in their support, because there was an alliance between Banu Qaynuqa' and the Khazraj. But the real truth was that the hypocrites were in fact brothers of the disbelieving People of the Book. After a great struggle, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agreed that instead of killing them they should be expelled, and that they could take with them their wealth and goods, except weapons. And these people went to Syria.

This was the event to which this verse alludes: that the Banu Nadir are like the Banu Qaynuqa', and the hypocrites are their brothers, and were also the brothers of those others. The hypocrites deceived their brothers, the disbelieving People of the Book, saying that they should resist, and that they (the hypocrites) were with them. But the outcome for them was this, and they did not stand by them at all. Here a perpetual parable is given of them: that whatever the hypocrites do, Satan does exactly the same, and those who follow Satan's advice meet a very evil end.

The passage is Urdu commentary; I translate it faithfully.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verses 16–17:

"Their example is that of Satan, who says to man, 'Disbelieve.' And when he has disbelieved, Satan says, 'I am free of you; indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.' Then the end of both will be that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein forever, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers." (59:16–17)

Satan's treatment of human beings is the same treatment that the hypocrites show towards the disbelievers among the People of the Book. Yet people still follow his words. This is a permanent reality, and the Qur'an, through this particular event, states it here so that from this partial incident a lasting and universal lesson and wisdom may be drawn, and the scope of the matter becomes broad, and the matter is not confined to a single particular event. It is the way of the Qur'an that it expresses lasting and sublime truths also through a particular instance, because purely universal and principled statements become dry philosophy, and they do not have the same effect on human consciousness, heart and mind as they do in the form of an example and an event. This is the difference between the style of expression of the Qur'an and the style of the philosophers and teachers. Philosophers speak only in the form of formulas.

The story of Banu Nadir ends with this example, and within this story the Qur'an has presented so many truths, guidance and images, and because of them this particular story has been made universal, or sublime truths have been presented in the form of this story. This event kept going on the earth while it kept working to reform the human conscience. Thus this event became more than an event: it became a lesson, a source of wisdom, a cause of guidance and admonition. The manner of expressing this event and these truths in the Book of Allah is something else, and the way humans express them is something else.

After this account of the Banu Nadir, this commentary on it, and the statement of great truths and guidance within it, the address now turns back to the believers, and they are addressed with that beloved word and beloved attribute: "O you who believe," so that they may accept it quickly and act upon it with ease. They are told: adopt the path of taqwa (God-consciousness); see what you have prepared for tomorrow, for the Day of Resurrection; do not forget Allah, as the earlier people forgot Him, so Allah made them forget themselves. Those people met an evil end and became people of the Fire.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 18:

یایھا الذین ........................ الفائزون (02) (95 : 81 تا 02) "O you who have believed, fear Allah, and let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow. Fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do. And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient. Not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise – they are the attainers (of success)." 

What is taqwa (God-consciousness)? It is a state of the heart, to which the very word only points. But words are not able to portray the reality of the state of taqwa. It is a state in which the heart is awake and sensitive, and possesses a keen awareness of Allah, and this awareness is present in every condition. A person is fearful of Allah, highly cautious, and feels shame before the prospect that Allah should find him in a state that does not please Him, for Allah sees every moment, and so no one can escape from Allah.

ولتنظر .................... لغد (95 : 81) "let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow." This is an expression whose meaning is far broader than its words, and upon hearing these words, the pages of a book open before the human imagination, in which all of one's deeds are recorded, small and great. So a person thinks about what preparations he has made for the entry of his deeds into the pages of that book. This very thought brings his own shortcomings before him, and many faults and sins come before him, even though he may have done good deeds and also striven in the path of truth. But what if his good deeds turned out to be few? Nevertheless, if these few words remain before a person, he can never become heedless. He will keep his deeds under constant watch.

After giving this awareness, the believers are further awakened.

واتقوا اللہ ................ تعملون (95 : 81) "Fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do." In this way, the sensitivity of the believing heart becomes keener. It fears, and while committing disobedience it feels shame before Allah, because Allah is aware of all of a person's deeds.

In light of the reminder and awakening called for in this verse, in the next verse they are admonished not to be like those who forgot Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 19:

﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves.﴾ This is a strange condition: that a person should forget himself, yet this is the reality. For whoever forgets Allah lives in this world in the manner that grazing animals live. Thus he forgets his human station, and from this reality there follows another reality. That is, having forgotten himself, he does not prepare any provision for his long life, and there is no preparation on his part for tomorrow.

﴿Those are the defiant transgressors.﴾ They have deviated from the path of truth and have gone outside the circle of Islam. For this reason, the next verse states that such people are among the people of Hell. And since the believers are the people of Paradise, they should adopt a path opposite to the path of those people, because the two paths are indeed separate.

﴿Not equal are the companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise are the ones who are successful.﴾ (95:02) The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise cannot be alike. Only those who enter Paradise are truly successful. Neither their circumstances are equal, nor their temperaments. Neither their path, nor the way they walk upon it. Neither their direction, nor their destination. In short, nothing about them can be equal. Their paths are separate, and they are so separate that they never meet at any point. Their direction is different, their line is different, whether in politics, in ranks, in this world, or in the Hereafter.

﴿The companions of Paradise are the ones who are successful.﴾ (95:02) Here the end of the people of Paradise is described, while the people of Hell are left out, since their end is already known. It is as if they have been forgotten and reduced to nothing.

Now comes the final and severe blow upon the strings of the heart and the sight, one that makes a person tremble. It is said: O believing heart, if this Qur'an had been sent down upon mountains, they too would have been shattered to pieces.

This is a parable, but a truth is presented at length as an illustration. This Qur'an has a great weight. It possesses tremendous power and boundless influence, and nothing can remain firm before it. Upon whomever its weight falls, he is shaken and reduced to pieces. When Hadrat Umar (رضي الله عنه) first recited it, he was shattered, and when he was listening to it from someone reciting it one night...

﴿By the Mount [Tur], and by a Book inscribed on parchment unrolled, and by the House frequented, and by the raised canopy, and by the sea filled with fire; indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to occur, for which there is no preventer.﴾ (52:1-7) So Hadrat Umar (رضي الله عنه) leaned against a wall and sat down. Afterwards he returned home and became so grief-stricken that people worshipped him for a month.

There are moments when a person's heart opens up to the insights of the Qur'an, and the effect of the Qur'an becomes so intense that the person is shaken, a trembling overtakes him, and such changes and transformations occur within him as magnets and electricity have their effect on iron and on the body, rather, an effect even more intense than that.

Allah is the Creator of the mountains and also the Revealer of the Qur'an. The command of Allah is:

﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split apart out of fear of Allah.﴾ (59:21) Those who have felt the effects of the Qur'an of this nature in their bodies can understand this reality, but their taste and feeling cannot be expressed in words.

And at the end of this surah comes the praise and glorification of the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate God. When the Qur'an has some effect upon a person's self, he begins to glorify Allah, and these beautiful names are such that their effects are clearly visible in the universe, because the attributes and names of Allah are seen in the manifestations of the cosmos and in its motion:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 22:

"He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity; the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity: the King, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him. He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. To Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise." (59:22-24)

The glorification of Allah has three parts, and each begins with the affirmation of the doctrine of Tawhid.

It begins with "Huwa Allahu la ilaha illa Huwa" or "Huwa Allah." Every one of Allah's Names has an effect that is clearly visible in this universe or in human life. This shows that the Being of Allah is active, and Allah's activity is connected with this universe and the lives of human beings. These are not negative attributes, nor are they separate from the practical side of this life. These attributes are with us in our environment, our circumstances, and our phenomena.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 59, verse 23:

﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity﴾ (59:22). Therefore, believe in His divinity, worship Him alone, and turn to Him alone when calling upon Him. From creation until death, He is the one who is effective and active in your life, and upon this belief the entire Islamic system of thought and system of action is established. The relations of people with one another, people's relations with the living creatures in general, and people's relations with this universe have all been built upon the foundation of the belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of God).

﴿...He knows the unseen and the seen﴾ (59:22): "He knows the unseen and the manifest." The purpose of this is to create the awareness that Allah is watching everything. Both the apparent and the hidden are manifest to Him. Therefore, a person should keep fresh the consciousness that He is watching, and then do whatever he wishes to do, because a human being does not live alone here, even when a person is in solitude. If a person develops this state within himself, then his heart can neither become heedless nor fall asleep.

﴿He is the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful﴾ (59:22). Through the conception of these attributes, a person becomes content and happy, and along with fear there is also hope. Tranquility comes along with awe. According to the concepts of the believers, Allah does not merely pursue people at every moment, but also oversees them. He does not merely give punishment and torment to people at every moment, but also guides them. They have not been left unattended like aimless beasts; rather, Allah guides them and also provides them assistance.

﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity﴾ (59:23). In this second glorification too, this belief, or the testimony of faith, has been repeated, because it is the fundamental principle.

﴿The King﴾ (59:23): The very deity other than whom there is no other deity is also the King. When He is also the King, it is necessary that in all matters recourse be to Him alone. There will be no other king then. Therefore, no person can accept two kings. Allah has not created two hearts in one person at the same time.

﴿The Holy﴾ (59:23): This word expresses utmost purity, absolute sanctity. Since Allah is the Most Holy, the hearts of Allah's servants should also be pure, so that Allah's pure teachings can settle within them and they become worthy of the descent of blessings and bounties, and are able to proclaim the purity of Allah.

﴿The Source of Peace﴾ (59:23): From the attribute of As-Salam there descends peace, security, and tranquility, and this entire universe is filled with safety. The heart of the believer becomes content from its Lord. Within the sanctuary of mercy of the one Allah, a person lives in peace. Then in this universe he finds himself secure from calamities and afflictions as well. His restlessness, unease, and all fatigue are removed, and he becomes a friend of everything in this universe.

﴿The Giver of Security﴾ (59:23): He grants security and safety. From this attribute it becomes clear what the significance of faith is: by becoming a believer, a human being shares in one of the attributes of Allah, and thus, after faith, he no longer remains a creature of the earth but rises toward the higher world.

﴿The Guardian﴾ (59:23): This is the distinctive aspect of the concept of Allah's attributes. The preceding attributes, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, and Al-Mu'min, are attributes related to His essence, but the attribute of Al-Muhaymin relates to the entire universe, and through it the watchfulness and sovereignty of Allah are manifested.

Similarly, the following attributes:

﴿The Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic﴾ (59:23): These are attributes through which Allah's grip, dominance, and compulsion are manifested. Through them is expressed a supremacy, power, and exaltation that has no partner. In truth, there is no partner in Allah's essence or attributes. He alone is Al-Aziz, He alone is Al-Jabbar, He alone is Al-Mutakabbir. These attributes cannot be applied to anyone other than Him.

This is why the surah concludes thus:

﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ (59:23): "Holy is Allah above the partners they ascribe."

And the final glorification is the longest: ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾ (95:43). ﴿He is the one God, and there is no other.﴾

﴿The Creator, the Originator﴾ (95:42): the one who plans creation and puts that plan into effect. Khalq (creation) means planning and designing the whole system of decree. Bari' means continually executing that plan. These two attributes are closely connected, and the difference between them is subtle.

﴿The Fashioner﴾ (95:42): the one who gives form. This attribute is also linked to the two before it. That is, there is a plan, then creation, then giving shape and determining features: fixing the form and nature of everything, and granting each thing its properties.

The continuous mention of these attributes here, which differ only slightly and are different stages of creation, indicates that this same gradual process operates in every act of creation. This indication is being given to human beings. According to human conceptions, a blueprint comes first, then creation, then shaping. In reality, with Allah there are no degrees and no stages; there is only ﴿Be, and it is﴾. We human beings understand these matters by bringing them within the scope of our own needs, and our power and capacity are very small.

﴿To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names﴾ (95:42). These names are good in themselves; they do not need to be called good by anyone for them to be good. These Asma al-Husna (the Most Beautiful Names) pour the bounties of beauty upon human hearts. By reflecting on them, and by developing these qualities within oneself and taking guidance from them, a person can attain perfection, because Allah loves to be described by these attributes. They are therefore praiseworthy attributes and commendable qualities. Accordingly, a person should keep rising to higher levels.

This long chain of glorifying, purifying and remembering Allah through His Most Beautiful Names now spreads across the vast expanse of the entire universe, for everything in the heavens and the earth receives these bounties. So you too should take lessons and benefit from these glorifications.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ (95:42). This is the scene that is expected after the mention of these attributes. All things share in it. The beginning and the end of the surah also come together: at the beginning there is the purification of Allah, and at the end His glorification, Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him).
